title: ABI Negotiation Protocol and Shim Generator for Non-breaking Runtime Evolution
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: We continue to observe customer breakage when shipping runtime improvements that change call framing, default kernel behavior, or optional capability flags. Many downstream SDKs implicitly rely on runtime defaults or behaviour that we consider internal. Past mitigations (long deprecation windows, semver notes) are insufficient because consumers sometimes need fast fixes and we lack automated adapter tooling.

Proposal: Define an explicit ABI Negotiation Protocol (ANP) v1 that is exchanged in every request/response as a compact header blob (machine-readable). Implement:
- A stable header format carrying 'abi-version', 'capabilities' bitset, and an 'opt-in-shim' token.
- Server-side negotiation: runtime accepts ranges and returns an effective ABI vector and migration hints.
- A developer tool 'abi-shimgen' that generates small, testable adapters (shims) for common breaking patterns (parameter name changes, enum remaps, KV-cache semantics).
- Rollout gates that require successful negotiation telemetry and canary-scope enforcement by customer, model, or region.

Goals: reduce user-facing breakages, shorten migration windows with automated adapters, and make breaking changes explicit and reversible without forcing major version bumps for minor internal improvements.
acceptance_criteria: Header spec published: 'X-Redwood-ABI' format and grammar documented in runtime RFC
Runtime parses and responds to header with deterministic negotiation outcome for >=95% synthetic cases
abi-shimgen CLI prototype generates shims for at least three canonical break scenarios and unit-tests
Integration tests showing zero-request failures during canary rollout when shim applied
Telemetry dashboard surfaces negotiation mismatches and shim adoption rates
Console UI exposes per-customer rollout toggle and automatic fallback policy
tasks: Write runtime RFC: header format, negotiation rules, and decision table
Implement header parsing and negotiation kernel in serving runtime
Build abi-shimgen: generator + template library for common mappings
Create migration catalog: canonical break scenarios and recommended shims
Add negotiation telemetry and alerts to observability pipeline
Create console rollout controls and per-customer toggles
End-to-end tests and canary plan for runtime-1.20
Security review and threat model for header integrity and opt-in tokens

2025-02-25: Decided on compact header binary-encoded vs JSON string; opted for CBOR-like binary for size and parsing speed
2025-02-28: Prototype header parser landed in runtime dev branch; basic negotiation table implemented

2025-03-05: Telemetry schema submitted to infra; canary plan drafted (stages: internal->beta customers->regional canaries)

comments: Evan Park: Strong +1 to shipping a generator — PMs have seen multiple customers stuck for weeks migrating SDKs.
Caroline Moss: Please ensure ABI headers are surfaced in SDK logs and error messages so developers can self-diagnose.
